subject: HIS
label: Grade 12 Humanities
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Humanities History, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Themes in ancient and medieval history
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Themes in ancient and medieval history', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: compare societies using sources. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Place it: find where and when 'Themes in ancient and medieval history' happens, on a map, a timeline or in a local example.
Gather: read or listen to two short sources and note who is speaking and why.
Use it: compare societies using sources. Give a reason and one piece of evidence for every point.
Weigh it: say what another person might think, and why, before you decide.
modules.example: Model run for 'Themes in ancient and medieval history'. Question: what happened, or what is the situation, and why? Sources: two short extracts, a map or table. Notes: who, what, where, when, why. Answer: three sentences, each with a reason and a piece of evidence. Check: is there a point of view that you have not considered? What a good answer looks like: facts are correct, reasons are linked to evidence, and one other point of view is named fairly.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Compare societies using sources: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Themes in ancient and medieval history), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Source work and historiography) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: talk about family, place and community.
L2: read maps and timelines; describe local government and history.
L4: analyse causes and consequences; argue from evidence.
L5: specialise in history, geography, politics or economics; write extended answers.
L6 (degree): research methods and applied social science.
L7 (postgraduate): policy, research or teaching at depth.
